first.rationale: Current situation shows simultaneous competitive pressure (aggressive entry pricing from competitor), activation decline (6% QoQ), and onboarding completion decline (4% QoQ). Memory_73 demonstrates promotional pricing effectively addresses price-sensitive SMBs with acquisition and revenue lift while improving time-to-first-value. Memory_31 shows onboarding simplification works but is orthogonal to the immediate competitive threat. Since activation and onboarding are both down, the root issue may be price sensitivity driving away cost-conscious segments rather than friction—the competitor's aggressive entry pricing is the direct threat. Promotional pricing can directly compete on the price axis while memory_31 and memory_91 address engagement, which are secondary to retention under competitive siege. Verifying memory_31 and memory_73 will confirm the magnitude of onboarding and pricing effects respectively to validate this priority ordering. Running a standard_experiment with promotional_pricing targets the acute competitive threat while preserving the option to layer activation or onboarding improvements later if the pricing experiment does not fully recover the 6% activation decline.
